newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr set for new attack on key yen levels.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr set for new attack on key yen levels.

text.p: The dollar, after setting a 44-month high at 115.08 yen, is ready to launch a fresh assault on a series of important resistance levels against the Japanese yen in thin year-end trading volume, analysts said on Thursday.
The dollar, could march through the 115.10-, 115.55- and 115.90-yen levels in a rapid-fire progression, they added.
Such gains would likely lift the dollar against other major currencies, they also predicted.
In late New York trade on Thursday, the dollar was quoted at 1.5528/38 marks, 114.88/98 yen and 1.3430/40 Swiss francs.

Chris Turner, senior currency strategist at I.D.E.A., said the dollar enjoyed solid support at "1.5510/20 marks, 114.40/yen and 1.3410/20 Swiss francs" and predicted that any "major move would be yen-led."
The scope for action is far more limited on dollar/mark with the U.S. currency stubbornly confined to the 1.5290- to 1.5730-mark range.
"It's all yen led," Turner said. "In a thin market, you might see some yen cross moves."
Mark/yen has been grinding higher to intermediate resistance at 73.80 from where it is ready to target 74.35.
Turner noted a mark/yen trendline from the 1995 lows comes in at 74.10.
"As we get closer to that level, mark/yen could race higher, and dollar/yen would follow. But dollar/mark would then move sideways or lower," the I.D.E.A. analyst said.

"Europe was closed during the major moves versus the yen which prevented the European currencies from gaining as much ground as dollar/yen did," added Turner who anticipated fresh gains by the European currencies versus the yen.
Trading resumed in the United States on Thursday after a one-day holiday for Christmas.
Most European marketplaces, except Paris, remained closed for Boxing Day and will resume trading on Friday.

"There might be some mark/yen activity going on," said Turner who expected further yen weakness due to the bearish outlook for "the weak financial system in Japan where interest rates cannot be raised anytime soon."
"The yen, again, is the great vehicle to borrow in," the I.D.E.A. analyst noted.
Wall Street analysts pointed out dollar/Swiss is looking very bullish and likely to soon test 1.35 -- a 19-month bull channel.
"Dollar/Swiss broke 1.3415/20 Tuesday in America. But Europe has not traded dollar/Swiss yet due to the (Christmas/Boxing Day) holiday," Turner noted.
"It will be very interesting to see what Europe does with dollar/Swiss at this level," he added. "It looks constructive and is supposed to go higher."
But some analysts cautioned that, dollar/Swiss -- often a good leader of overall trends -- may run out of steam at 1.35 even and fail to challenge the daunting 1.3555 level.
-- Isabelle Clary, 212-859-1666
